issues.legal_issue: A prior benefit to a selection committee chair does not establish that a later selection was tainted by mala fides when the benefit is unconnected to the candidates and the selection.
material_facts: A residential site was allotted to the committee chair before he became a member of the Commission and before the selection took place.
The allotment had been proposed by a senior state official and approved by the state government in recognition of the chair’s services to the state.
There was no evidence that any selected candidate had been involved in the allotment or that the allotment was connected to the selection.
issues.conclusion: The allegation of mala fides against the chair was far-fetched and was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Mala fides in a selection must be substantiated; courts must scrutinize such allegations carefully, particularly where an unsuccessful candidate has an interest in challenging the process. A remote prior benefit, without evidence connecting it to the selection or to the selected candidates, does not establish bias.

rule.if: selection_challenge and prior_benefit_preceded_selection and benefit_unconnected_to_candidates and no_direct_evidence_of_favoritism

predicates.selection_challenge: A person challenges a selection on the ground that it was affected by bias.
predicates.prior_benefit_preceded_selection: The decision-maker received a benefit before participating in the selection.
predicates.benefit_unconnected_to_candidates: No selected candidate was shown to have participated in or otherwise been connected to the benefit.
predicates.no_direct_evidence_of_favoritism: No direct evidence connected the benefit to favorable treatment in the selection.

issues.definition: When a selection challenge relies on a prior benefit that is unconnected to the candidates and lacks direct evidence of favoritism, the alleged mala fides are not established.

issues.legal_issue: A mala fides allegation against a decision-maker cannot be entertained when that person has not been made a party to the proceeding.
material_facts: A senior state official was accused of mala fides in connection with the selection.
That official had not been impleaded as a party before the Tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The allegation against the official could not be considered.
issues.legal_principle: An allegation of mala fides against a person cannot be entertained in the proceeding when that person has not been joined as a party.

predicates.selection_bias_claim: A party alleges that a decision-maker acted with mala fides in a selection.
predicates.accused_decision_maker_not_joined: The decision-maker accused of mala fides has not been made a party to the proceeding.

issues.definition: If a selection bias claim accuses a decision-maker who has not been joined to the proceeding, the claim is not entertained.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of a committee member other than its presiding Commission representative does not invalidate selection proceedings when more than half of the committee members attend.
material_facts: The post of a member who would ordinarily sit on the selection committee had been abolished.
Six of the seven committee members attended the selection meeting.
The absent member was not the chair or a member of the Commission.
issues.conclusion: The selection committee was properly constituted and its proceedings were valid.
issues.legal_principle: Regulation 3(3) of the Indian Administrative Service (Appointment by Promotion) Regulations, 1955 provides that the absence of a member other than the Chairman or a Member of the Commission does not invalidate committee proceedings if more than half of the members attend. The Court also found no prejudice from the absence in this case.

predicates.selection_committee_proceeding: A selection committee is conducting proceedings to assess candidates.
predicates.absent_member_not_presiding_commission_m: An absent committee member is neither the chair nor a member of the Commission who presides over the committee.
predicates.more_than_half_members_attended: More than half of the committee members attended the meeting.

issues.definition: When a selection committee meets without a non-presiding Commission member and more than half its members attend, its proceedings remain valid.

issues.legal_issue: A selection committee may consider service reports prepared late where the applicable service rules preserve their validity, and an officer should not lose consideration because the responsible reporting authority failed to prepare reports on time.
material_facts: Some annual service reports had been prepared after the deadline that applied under an earlier version of the service rules.
Later amendments removed the deadline, and the rules subsequently in force preserved matters duly done under the earlier rules.
The Selection Committee considered the reports in assessing the candidates.
issues.conclusion: The reports were not required to be ignored, and considering them did not constitute a statutory breach.
issues.legal_principle: The Karnataka Civil Services (Performance Reports) Rules, 1994, as amended in 1999, removed the relevant time limit retrospectively; the 2000 Rules preserved matters done under the earlier rules. An officer should not suffer because the authority responsible for preparing or reviewing a report failed to do so within time.

predicates.promotion_selection_proceeding: The proceeding concerns selection for promotion to a public service.
predicates.service_rules_preserve_late_reports: The applicable service rules preserve the validity of reports prepared late under the governing framework.
predicates.candidate_not_responsible_for_reporting_: The delay in preparing the reports resulted from the reporting or reviewing authority rather than the candidate.

issues.definition: In a promotion selection, late service reports may be considered when the governing rules preserve them and the candidate did not cause the delay.

issues.legal_issue: A selection committee may obtain and consider a special service report when ordinary annual reports are unavailable, and the candidate should not be penalized for the reporting authority’s failure to prepare those reports.
material_facts: Annual reports for some years were unavailable because the reporting or reviewing authorities had not prepared them.
A special report was obtained for a candidate whose ordinary reports were missing.
The Selection Committee considered that special report in assessing the candidate.
issues.conclusion: Obtaining and considering the special report was a permissible administrative practice and was not arbitrary or discriminatory.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 11-A of the Karnataka Civil Services (Performance Reports) (Amendment) Rules, 1996 permitted the appointing authority to direct preparation of reports for periods for which reports were unavailable. The Court also recognized that special reports may be obtained in administrative practice so that an officer does not suffer from an authority’s failure to complete reporting.

predicates.promotion_selection_proceeding: The proceeding concerns selection for promotion to a public service.
predicates.annual_reports_unavailable: Ordinary annual service reports are missing for one or more relevant periods.
predicates.special_report_obtained_for_missing_peri: The authority obtains a special report addressing a period for which an ordinary report is unavailable.
predicates.candidate_not_responsible_for_missing_re: The missing reports resulted from the reporting or reviewing authority rather than the candidate.

issues.definition: When ordinary reports are missing through no fault of the candidate, a special report obtained to address the gap may be considered in the promotion selection.

issues.legal_issue: Courts and tribunals do not sit as appellate authorities over expert selection committees’ comparative assessments unless the selection is affected by mala fides, a serious breach of statutory rules, or an apparent error.
material_facts: The Selection Committee scrutinized candidates’ service records and interviewed them under a prescribed marking system.
The Committee made an overall comparative assessment, including assessments that differed from those of reporting or reviewing officers.

The Tribunal questioned the grading of candidates and set aside selections, but the record did not establish mala fides, a serious statutory breach, or an apparent error in the Committee’s assessment.
issues.conclusion: The courts and Tribunal could not substitute their assessment for that of the Selection Committee, and the selections could not be set aside on the grounds raised.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the limited judicial-review approach reflected in R.S. Dass v. Union of India, Union Public Service Commission v. Hiranyalal Dev, Dalpat Abasaheb Solunke v. Dr. B.S. Mahajan, National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences v. Dr. K. Kalyana Raman, Anil Katiyar v. Union of India, Ramanand Prasad Singh v. Union of India, and Union Public Service Commission v. K. Rajaiah. The Selection Committee’s comparative assessment and grading are its function; courts and tribunals may not reassess candidates as an appellate body absent mala fides, statutory non-compliance, or apparent error. Regulation 5 of the applicable selection regulations governed the Committee’s assessment.

rule.if: candidate_selection_challenge and expert_committee_made_comparative_assessment and no_proven_mala_fides and no_serious_rule_violation and no_apparent_error

predicates.candidate_selection_challenge: A candidate challenges the outcome of a selection made by a duly constituted expert committee.
predicates.expert_committee_made_comparative_assess: The committee assessed candidates’ records and other relevant material comparatively.
predicates.no_proven_mala_fides: The evidence does not establish that the selection was affected by mala fides.
predicates.no_serious_rule_violation: The evidence does not establish a serious breach of the rules governing the selection.
predicates.no_apparent_error: The evidence does not establish an apparent error in the committee’s assessment.

issues.definition: When an expert committee has comparatively assessed candidates and there is no proven mala fides, serious rule violation, or apparent error, its assessment is not reopened as though on appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A screening committee’s shortlisting assessment should not be displaced when the record does not show that the excluded candidates were more meritorious than those shortlisted.
material_facts: The Screening Committee reviewed the service records of eligible officers and shortlisted candidates for consideration by the Selection Committee.
Two candidates challenged their exclusion from the shortlist.
The record did not show that the shortlisted candidates were less meritorious than the excluded candidates.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the non-shortlisting of those candidates was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the High Court’s conclusion that the Screening Committee had assessed the candidates’ records and that there was no evidence that the shortlisted candidates were not meritorious. The limited judicial-review principles governing expert selection assessments applied.

predicates.shortlisting_challenge: An applicant challenges exclusion from a shortlist for further selection.
predicates.screening_committee_assessed_records: The screening committee assessed applicants’ records in deciding whom to shortlist.
predicates.no_evidence_excluded_candidates_more_mer: The record does not show that the excluded applicants were more meritorious than those shortlisted.

issues.definition: When a screening committee has assessed applicants’ records and there is no evidence that excluded applicants were more meritorious, its shortlisting decision is not displaced.

issues.legal_issue: A contempt petition lacks merit when the underlying appeals are dismissed and the Court finds no independent basis for contempt.
material_facts: The contempt petition arose from the same selection dispute as the civil appeals.
The Court dismissed the civil appeals after finding no merit in the challenges to the selection.
issues.conclusion: The contempt petition was dismissed as lacking merit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court dismissed the contempt petition in view of its decision in the civil appeals and its finding that the petition had no merit.

predicates.contempt_proceeding_related_to_selection: A contempt proceeding arises from the same dispute as appeals challenging a selection.
predicates.underlying_appeals_dismissed: The appeals underlying the contempt proceeding have been dismissed.
predicates.no_independent_contempt_basis_found: The Court identifies no separate basis for granting the contempt petition.

issues.definition: When a related contempt proceeding has no independent basis and the underlying appeals are dismissed, the contempt petition is dismissed.
